Call us from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**. If you are already using a Northline phone, dial **611**. Our support team is available **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. We're ready to answer any questions about moving your number.

title: Move your number to another carrier
body_text:
# Move your number to another carrier
You can keep your phone number when you switch to a new carrier. Follow these steps to share the information they need.

## What you need
- Your Northline account number. This is the number that identifies your Northline account.
- A Transfer PIN. This is a short code that lets the new carrier move your number. The PIN works for 7 days after you create it.

## Get your Transfer PIN
1. Open the My Northline app on your phone.
2. Tap **Security** in the menu.
3. Choose **Transfer PIN**.
4. The app will show a six-digit PIN. Write it down or keep the screen visible.

The PIN is only good for 7 days, so give it to the new carrier soon. If you lose the PIN, repeat the steps to create a new one.

## Give the PIN to your new carrier
1. Call the new carrier's transfer department or use their online portal.
2. Provide them with your Northline account number and the Transfer PIN you just created.
3. The new carrier will complete the number move while the PIN is still valid.

If you have any trouble, remember that Northline support agents cannot read a Transfer PIN over the phone. Only the account security team can handle PIN requests. You will need to use the app to get a new PIN if the old one expires.

## Need more help?
Call Northline support from your Northline phone by dialing **611**, or from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline app** or at **northline.example**.

title: Change your phone number
body_text:
# Change your phone number
You can change the phone number on your Northline Wireless account for free once every 12 months.

## How to request a number change
1. Open the **My Northline** app on your phone, or go to **northline.example** in a web browser.
2. Sign in with your account username and password.
3. Tap **Account** then **Phone Number**.
4. Choose **Change Number**.
5. Follow the prompts to type the new number you want.
6. Confirm the change.
If you have trouble in the app or on the website, call support. Tell the representative you want to change your phone number. They will complete the request for you.

## What happens after the change
- The old number stops working **right away**. Calls to the old number will not connect.
- Your voicemail messages stay with the old number and are **not moved** to the new one. You will need to set up new voicemail for the new number.
- The change does not affect your monthly bill. Your plan and any add-ons stay the same.

## Things to remember
- You can only change your number **once every 12 months**. The change is free.
- If you need to keep voicemail from the old number, record the messages before you change, then set up new voicemail after the change.
- Your account has no contract or early termination fee, so the number change will not create any extra charges.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**, or dial **611** from your Northline phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. They can walk you through the number change or answer any questions.

title: Cancel your service
body_text:
# Cancel your service

You can stop your Northline Wireless service when you need to. Follow these steps to finish the process.

## Who can cancel

Only the account owner may request a cancellation. The account owner is the person whose name is on the bill. If you are not the owner, you will need to ask them to cancel for you.

## How to cancel

You can cancel using the My Northline app or the website at northline.example.

1. Open the My Northline app or go to northline.example and sign in with your username and password.
2. Tap or click **Account** then **Settings**.
3. Choose **Cancel Service**.
4. Confirm that you are the account owner when asked.
5. Follow the on-screen prompts to finish the request.

If you prefer to speak with a person, call support:

- Dial **611** from any Northline phone, or
- Call **1-800-555-0199** from any other phone.

Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

## What happens after you cancel

- Your service will stop at the end of the current billing month. A billing month is the month you have already paid for in advance.
- Northline does not charge an early termination fee. There is no extra cost for ending service early.
- You will receive a final bill for any usage up to the cancellation date.
- If the final bill shows a credit (money the carrier owes you), the credit will be refunded within **5 to 7 business days**. Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding holidays.

## Need more help?

Call us at **1-800-555-0199** or dial **611** from your Northline phone. Our team is ready to help from **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

title: When an account holder has died
body_text:
# When an account holder has died

If the person who owns a Northline Wireless account passes away, you can let the account team help you close or transfer the service.

## What the account team can do

The account team can either cancel the service or move ownership to a family member. They may ask you to send a copy of the death certificate, which is the official paper that proves someone has died. Northline Wireless does not have contracts or early-termination fees, so the account can be ended without extra charges. You will receive a reply within two business days after you open a case.

## How to start the process

1. Gather a clear copy of the death certificate.
2. Choose whether you want the service cancelled or transferred to another person.
3. Call support:
   - Dial **611** from any Northline phone, **or** call **1-800-555-0199** from any phone.
   - Call between **7 a.m. and 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.
4. Tell the representative you need help because the account holder has died.
5. Follow the representative's instructions for sending the death certificate (email, fax, or upload through the My Northline app).
6. Wait for the support team to open a case and reply, which should happen within two business days.

## What happens after the case is opened

- **If you cancel**: The account will be closed, and the final bill will be charged in advance for the month you are leaving.
- **If you transfer**: The new owner will be added to the account. They can manage the account in the My Northline app or at northline.example. All existing plans stay the same, and the new owner will start paying the monthly bill in advance.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support at **611** from a Northline phone or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. - 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline app** or online at **northline.example**.

title: Transfer account ownership
body_text:
# Transfer account ownership

You can move your Northline Wireless account to another person. Both people must agree, and the new owner will pay the bill.

## What the transfer means
Account ownership transfer changes who is responsible for the monthly bill. The new owner becomes the person who receives the bill and pays it. The old owner no longer has any responsibility for the account after the transfer is finished.

## How to start the transfer
1. **Both owners agree** - The current owner and the new owner must both say "yes" to the transfer.
2. **Contact Northline support** - Call 611 from a Northline phone, or call 1-800-555-0199 from any phone.
3. **Provide required information** - Tell the support agent the phone number(s) on the account, the name of the current owner, and the name of the new owner.
4. **Confirm the new owner's details** - The new owner should have a valid email address and a payment method ready for the monthly bill.

The support team will start the process after you finish these steps.

## What to expect after you request
- The account team will finish the transfer in **3 to 5 business days**. A business day is a normal work day (Monday-Friday) that is not a holiday.
- During this time, the account stays active and you can still use your phone.
- Once the transfer is complete, the new owner will receive the first bill and will be charged **in advance** for the upcoming month.
- You can check the status of the transfer in the **My Northline app** or at **northline.example**.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support at **1-800-555-0199** (or dial **611** from a Northline phone). Help is available **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account online with the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: Lost or stolen phone
body_text:
# Lost or stolen phone

If your phone is lost or stolen, act quickly to stop anyone from using it and to start the replacement process.

## 1. Suspend the line right away
1. Open the My Northline app on another device.
2. Tap **Devices**.
3. Choose the lost or stolen phone.
4. Tap **Suspend**.
5. Confirm the suspension.

If you cannot use the app, call **1-800-555-0199** from any other phone and tell the representative you need to suspend your line.

## 2. Block the device by its IMEI
The IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) is a unique number that identifies your phone. Northline will block the phone using this number so it cannot be used on any network. The block happens automatically when you suspend the line.

## 3. Replace the phone or SIM card
- **With Device Protection**: If you pay for the Device Protection add-on, the claims team will arrange a replacement phone for you. A deductible may apply, but the claim process is handled for you.
- **Without Device Protection**: You can still get a new phone on your own. You will need a new SIM card to activate it. A replacement SIM card costs **$10**.

To order a new SIM, call **1-800-555-0199** or use the app's "SIM replacement" option.

## Need more help?
Call Northline support at **611** from a Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open daily from **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**. You can also manage your account online in the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: Protect your number with Number Lock
body_text:
# Protect your number with Number Lock

Number Lock keeps your phone number from being moved to another carrier or another SIM. It is a free feature that you control in the My Northline app.

## What Number Lock does

Number Lock stops anyone from transferring your number without your permission. While it is turned on, the number cannot be moved to a different carrier or placed on a new SIM card. The feature does not affect your ability to make calls or send texts. It is meant to protect you from accidental or fraudulent number changes.

## Turn Number Lock on or off

1. Open the My Northline app on your phone.
2. Tap **Menu** (the three lines) and choose **Security**.
3. Find **Number Lock** in the list.
4. Tap the switch to turn it **On**. The switch will turn green or show "On".
5. If you need to move your number yourself, tap the switch again to turn it **Off**. The switch will show "Off".

The app will confirm each change with a short message.

## When to turn it off

Only turn Number Lock off when you are moving your number to another carrier or to a new SIM that you have purchased yourself. After the transfer is complete, you can turn Number Lock back on to keep the number safe. Leaving it off for any other reason may let someone else move your number without your knowledge.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline app** or at **northline.example**.

title: Pause your service
body_text:
# Pause your service

You can stop your Northline Wireless service for a short time, such as when you travel far away.

## When you can pause

- You may pause service for up to **90 days** in any 12-month period.
- The pause is only for the account owner to request.
- While the service is paused, your phone number stays the same, but calls, texts, and data will not work.

## How to request a pause

1. Pick up any phone and dial **1-800-555-0199** (or dial **611** if you are using a Northline phone).
2. When the support representative answers, tell them you want to **pause your service**.
3. Confirm the start date and the length of the pause. Remember it cannot be longer than 90 days.
4. The representative will note the request in your account.
5. Ask for a confirmation number and write it down for your records.

You can also send the request through the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example** if you prefer to manage your account online.

## What happens while paused

- Your monthly bill will still be charged in advance, as usual.
- Your phone will not be able to place calls, send texts, or use mobile data.
- Your phone number is kept, so you can use it again when you end the pause.
- When the pause period ends, service automatically resumes and you can use your phone normally.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support at **1-800-555-0199** (or **611** from a Northline phone). Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your request in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.

title: Phone shows no service
body_text:
# Phone shows no service

If your phone says "No Service," try these basic steps before calling support.

## Try simple fixes
1. **Restart the phone.** Hold the power button, select "Power off," wait a few seconds, then turn it on again.
2. **Toggle Airplane Mode.** Airplane mode is a setting that turns off all wireless signals. Turn it on, wait 10 seconds, then turn it off.
3. **Check for an outage.** Visit northline.example/outage on a computer or another device to see if Northline Wireless is reporting a network problem.
4. **Remove and reinsert the SIM card.** The SIM card is a small chip that lets your phone connect to the carrier. Power off the phone, take out the SIM, wait a moment, then put it back in and turn the phone on.

## Check your account
1. Open the **My Northline** app or go to northline.example and sign in.
2. Look at your bill status. If the bill is past due, the service may be paused. Pay any overdue amount to restore service.

## When to call support
If none of the steps above restore service, contact Northline Wireless support. You can reach them by:

- Dialing **611** from any Northline phone, or
- Calling **1-800-555-0199** from any phone.

Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time, every day**. Have your account information ready, such as your phone number and the steps you already tried.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support at 1-800-555-0199 or dial 611 from your phone. Representatives are available 7 a.m.-9 p.m. Central Time, every day.

title: Calls go straight to voicemail
body_text:
# Calls go straight to voicemail

If your calls are landing in voicemail, something on the phone is stopping them from ringing.

## 1. Make sure Do Not Disturb is off
Do Not Disturb (DND) silences incoming calls. When it is on, a moon icon appears in the status bar.

1. Open the Settings app.
2. Tap **Do Not Disturb** (or **Focus** on some phones).
3. Turn the switch **off** so the moon icon disappears.

## 2. Turn off Airplane mode and call forwarding
Airplane mode disables all wireless signals, including calls. Call forwarding sends your calls to another number, often voicemail.

1. Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the Quick Settings panel.
2. Look for the airplane icon; if it is highlighted, tap it to turn it **off**.
3. Open **Settings** > **Phone** (or **Calls**) > **Call Forwarding**.
4. If any number is listed, select **Turn off** or **Disable**.

## 3. Verify the caller is not blocked
A blocked number is prevented from reaching you and will go straight to voicemail.

1. Open **Settings** > **Phone** > **Blocked Contacts** (or **Blocked Numbers**).
2. Review the list. If the person who is calling is there, swipe left on their name and tap **Unblock**.

After you have checked these three areas, try a test call from another phone. If the call rings, the problem is solved. If it still goes to voicemail, there may be a network issue or a setting we missed.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.

title: Mobile data is slow
body_text:
# Mobile data is slow

If your phone feels slow when you use the internet, it may be because you have used all the data your plan provides.

## Check your data usage

1. Open the My Northline app.
2. Look for the "Data Used" or "Usage" screen.
3. If the amount shown equals the amount in your plan, your speed will be reduced.

*Data* is the amount of internet you can download or upload each month. When you reach the limit, the carrier slows the connection.

## Try simple fixes

1. Turn your phone off and on again. This is called a restart and can clear temporary problems.
2. If you have a Wi-Fi network at home or work, connect to it. *Wi-Fi* is a wireless internet connection that does not use your mobile data.

Using Wi-Fi can make web pages load faster and save your mobile data for when you are away from home.

## Add a Data Top-Up

If you need full speed right away, you can buy a Data Top-Up.

1. In the My Northline app, tap **Add-On** or **Buy More Data**.
2. Choose **Data Top-Up 5**.
3. Confirm the purchase. The top-up costs $10 one time and adds 5 GB of data.

The extra 5 GB works until the end of your current billing month, after which your regular plan limits apply again.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support at **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: Cannot send or receive texts
body_text:
# Cannot send or receive texts

If your messages are not going through, try these simple steps. They often fix the problem.

## Check signal and number

1. Look at the signal bars on your phone. If there are no bars, you have weak or no signal. Move to a window or go outside for better reception.
2. Open the message you want to send. Make sure the phone number includes the three-digit area code (the first three numbers of the local region). A missing area code can stop the text from delivering.

## Restart the phone and free storage

1. Press and hold the power button until the screen asks to turn off. Choose "Power off," wait a few seconds, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears temporary glitches.
2. If your phone says it is full, delete old photos, apps, or messages you no longer need. Freeing storage gives the phone room to create new text messages.

## Picture messages need mobile data

Picture messages (MMS) are different from regular texts. They require mobile data, which is the internet connection that your carrier provides over the cellular network.

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Find **Mobile data** (sometimes called **Cellular data**) and make sure it is turned **On**.
3. If you are on a plan with no data, picture messages will not send until you add a data plan or use Wi-Fi.

## When to contact Northline Wireless

If the steps above do not help, the issue may be with your account or the network. Northline Wireless support can check for outages or account blocks.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless from your phone by dialing **611**, or from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: Cannot make calls
body_text:
# Cannot make calls

If you cannot place a call, follow these simple checks to find the problem and fix it.

## Check basic phone settings
1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Look for **Airplane Mode** and make sure it is turned **off**. (Airplane mode stops all wireless signals.)
3. Return to the home screen and see if the signal bar icons appear at the top. More bars mean a stronger cellular signal.

## Verify your account is current
1. Open the **My Northline** app or log in at northline.example.
2. Look for the bill status. If the bill is more than 30 days past due, calls may be blocked.
3. Pay any overdue amount to restore service.

## Restart the phone
1. Press and hold the power button until the power menu appears.
2. Choose **Restart** (or turn the phone off, wait a few seconds, then turn it back on).
3. After the phone powers up, try making a call again.

## Try Wi-Fi calling when indoors
If the signal bars are weak inside your home, you can use **Wi-Fi calling** (making calls over your internet connection).
1. Open **Settings** > **Phone** > **Wi-Fi Calling**.
2. Turn the feature **on**.
3. Connect to your home Wi-Fi network and place the call.

If none of these steps work, the issue may be with the network or your device.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is available **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or online at northline.example.

title: Calls keep dropping
body_text:
# Calls keep dropping

If your calls end unexpectedly, try these simple steps. They often fix the problem.

## Check signal and coverage

1. Look at the signal bars on your phone. Low bars can cause drops.
2. Go to **northline.example/coverage** on a computer or another device. This page shows where Northline Wireless has strong service.
3. If you are in an area with weak coverage, move to a spot with better signal, such as near a window.

## Turn on Wi-Fi calling

Wi-Fi calling lets your phone use a home internet connection for calls when the cellular signal is weak.

1. Open the phone's Settings app.
2. Tap **Phone** (or **Cellular**) and find **Wi-Fi Calling**.
3. Switch the toggle to **On**.
4. Follow any on-screen prompts to confirm.

Now you can place calls over Wi-Fi, which helps indoors.

## Update your phone's software

Out-of-date software can cause call problems.

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **General** then **Software Update** (or **System Update**).
3. If an update is available, tap **Download and Install**.
4. Let the phone restart when it asks.

Keeping the software current improves reliability.

## Gather details for support

When you call support, give them clear information.

1. Write down the exact places where calls drop (e.g., "kitchen, 3 p.m.").
2. Note how often it happens (every call, every few minutes, etc.).
3. Keep your phone's model and the software version handy.

Having these details speeds up the fix.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at **northline.example**.

title: Phone will not turn on
body_text:
# Phone will not turn on

If your phone does not power up, follow these steps to try to fix it.

## Check the battery

1. Find a charging cable that you know works with another device.
2. Plug the cable into a wall outlet and connect it to your phone.
3. Let the phone charge for at least 30 minutes.

A battery that is completely empty can prevent the phone from turning on. Charging for half an hour gives the battery enough power to start.

## Perform a hard reset

1. After the phone has charged, locate the power button (the button that turns the phone on and off).
2. Press and hold the power button for 20 seconds.
3. Release the button and wait a few seconds.

Holding the power button for a longer time forces the phone to restart its internal hardware. If the screen lights up, the phone is working again.

## Use Device Protection if needed

If the phone still does not start and you have **Device Protection** (a service that covers loss, theft, and damage for $9 a month), you can ask the claims team for help. The claims team will guide you through repair or replacement options. A deductible applies to each claim.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**, or dial **611** if you are using a Northline phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: Voicemail is not working
body_text:
# Voicemail is not working

If you cannot leave or hear new voicemail messages, follow these steps to fix it.

## Why voicemail may stop working
A full mailbox blocks new messages. Northline Wireless voicemail can store up to 30 messages. When the box is full, callers cannot leave a new greeting.

## Delete old messages
1. Open the Phone app on your device.
2. Tap the Voicemail icon.
3. Look for a list of saved messages.
4. Press and hold a message you want to remove, then select **Delete**.
5. Repeat until you have fewer than 30 messages stored.

Removing old messages frees space for new ones.

## Reset your voicemail PIN
The voicemail PIN (personal identification number) is the code you type to hear your messages. If the PIN is wrong, you cannot access voicemail.

1. Open the **My Northline** app.
2. Tap **Devices** in the menu.
3. Choose **Voicemail**.
4. Select **Reset PIN** and follow the on-screen prompts to create a new four-digit code.

After resetting, try calling your own number to check voicemail.

## Make sure call forwarding is off
Call forwarding sends incoming calls to another number, which can also stop voicemail from working.

1. Open the Phone app.
2. Tap the three-dot menu and choose **Settings**.
3. Find **Call forwarding** and tap it.
4. If any forwarding option is turned on, switch it to **Off**.

With forwarding disabled, calls will go to your voicemail when you do not answer.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open daily from **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.

title: Hotspot is not working
body_text:
# Hotspot is not working

If your phone's hotspot won't share internet, follow these steps to find the problem.

## Verify Your Plan

A hotspot only works if your plan includes hotspot data.
1. Look at your plan name. The plans **Northline Talk**, **Starter 1**, and **Everyday 5** have **0 GB hotspot** - they cannot use a hotspot.
2. If you have **Plus 10**, **Extra 20**, **Unlimited Essentials**, **Unlimited Premium**, or **Two-Line Unlimited**, your plan does include hotspot data.

If your plan does not include hotspot data, you will need to change to a plan that does or add a Hotspot Boost add-on.

## Check Hotspot Data Usage

Your hotspot may be turned off because you have used all the hotspot data for the month.
1. Open the **My Northline** app on your phone.
2. Tap the **Data** or **Hotspot** section.
3. See how many hotspot megabytes or gigabytes remain for the current month.

If the usage shows you have used all the allotted hotspot data, you must wait until the next billing cycle or add more hotspot data with a Hotspot Boost add-on.

## Restart Hotspot and Re-enter Password

Sometimes the connection just needs a reset.
1. Go to **Settings** > **Personal Hotspot** (or **Mobile Hotspot**) on your phone.
2. Turn the hotspot switch **Off**. Wait a few seconds.
3. Turn the hotspot switch **On** again.
4. On the device trying to connect (tablet, laptop, etc.), forget the hotspot network, then select it again and type the password exactly as shown in your phone's hotspot settings.

If the device still cannot connect, repeat the steps or try restarting both devices.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support from a Northline phone by dialing **611**, or from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.

title: Phone does not work abroad
body_text:
# Phone does not work abroad
If your Northline Wireless phone won't connect while you are outside the United States, follow these steps to fix it.

## Check your International Day Pass
1. Open the My Northline app or log in at northline.example.
2. Look for the International Day Pass add-on.
3. Make sure the add-on is active for the day you are traveling.
   - The International Day Pass costs $10 a day and is only charged on days you use the phone abroad.

If the pass is not on your account, you will not get data or roaming service.

## Turn on data roaming and restart
1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Find **Mobile Network** (or **Cellular**) and tap it.
3. Tap **Data Roaming** and switch it **On**.
   - *Data roaming* lets your phone use another carrier's network when you are outside the U.S.
4. Press the power button to turn the phone off, wait a few seconds, then turn it back on.

Restarting helps the phone register with the new network.

## Choose a network manually
If the phone still does not connect:

1. Open **Settings** again and go to **Mobile Network**.
2. Tap **Network Operators** (or **Carrier Selection**).
3. Turn off **Automatic** selection.
4. A list of available networks will appear.
5. Tap the name of a network you see (usually the strongest signal).

Your phone should now attach to that network and give you service.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support from any Northline phone by dialing **611**, or from any other phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: eSIM will not activate
body_text:
# eSIM will not activate

If your eSIM does not turn on, follow these simple steps. An eSIM is a digital SIM card that lets your phone connect to the network without a physical card.

## Check your connection
1. Open the Settings app on your phone.
2. Tap **Wi-Fi** and make sure it is turned on.
3. Connect to a Wi-Fi network you trust.
   *Wi-Fi* is a wireless internet connection that uses radio waves.

## Restart and retry
1. Press and hold the power button until the phone turns off.
2. Wait a few seconds, then turn the phone back on.
3. Open the **My Northline** app.
4. Go to **Devices** and select the eSIM you are trying to activate.
5. Tap **Activate** again.

## Wait for activation
- The activation process can take up to **15 minutes**.
- Do not close the app or turn off Wi-Fi while you wait.
- If the activation succeeds, you will see a confirmation message in the app.

## When to call support
1. If the activation fails a second time, note the error message.
2. Find your phone's **IMEI** number. The IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) is a unique code that identifies your device. You can see it in Settings > About phone, or on the box that came with the phone.
3. Call Northline Wireless support:
   - Dial **611** from any Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any other phone.
   - Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.
4. Tell the representative you have an eSIM activation problem and give them the IMEI.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support at **1-800-555-0199** (or **611** from a Northline phone) between **7 a.m. and 9 p.m. Central Time**, any day of the week. Have your IMEI ready when you call.

title: SIM card not detected
body_text:
# SIM card not detected

If your phone cannot see the SIM card, try these simple steps to fix it.

## Check the SIM card in your phone

1. Turn the phone off. This stops any power that could hurt the card.
2. Open the SIM tray (usually on the side of the phone).
3. Take the SIM card out.
4. Gently wipe the metal side of the SIM with a dry, soft cloth. Do not use water or chemicals.
5. Put the SIM back into the tray exactly as it was, then close the tray.
6. Turn the phone on again and see if the signal returns.

*SIM card*: a small plastic piece that holds your phone number and lets the phone talk to the network.

## Test the SIM in another phone

1. If the card still does not appear, place it in a different phone that works with Northline Wireless.
2. Turn that phone on.

- If the second phone also cannot read the SIM, the card is likely faulty.
- If the second phone works, the problem may be with the first phone's tray or antenna.

## Replace a faulty SIM

- A replacement physical SIM card costs $10.
- An electronic SIM (eSIM) can be set up for free and does not require a physical card.

To get a new SIM, you can request it through the My Northline app or at northline.example. The fee will be added to your next bill.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support from any phone at **1-800-555-0199** or dial **611** from a Northline phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or online.

title: Wi-Fi calling is not working
body_text:
# Wi-Fi calling is not working

If you cannot make calls over Wi-Fi, follow these simple steps to fix the problem.

## 1. Verify Wi-Fi calling is turned on and an emergency address is saved
Wi-Fi calling lets you place calls using a Wi-Fi network instead of the cellular signal.

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Find **Phone** or **Connections** (the name may vary).
3. Tap **Wi-Fi calling** and make sure the switch is **On**.
4. Look for **Emergency address** or **Location for 911**. If it is blank, enter your home address and save it.

## 2. Test a different Wi-Fi network
Sometimes the network you are using blocks Wi-Fi calling.

1. Go to a place with another Wi-Fi signal, such as a neighbor's house, a coffee shop, or a public library.
2. Connect your phone to that Wi-Fi network.
3. Try making a call. If it works, the original network may need a router reset or may not support Wi-Fi calling.

## 3. Update your phone's software and restart
Out-of-date software can stop Wi-Fi calling from working.

1. Open **Settings** and select **Software Update** (or **System Update**).
2. If an update is available, follow the prompts to download and install it.
3. After the update finishes, press and hold the power button, then choose **Restart** (or turn the phone off, wait a few seconds, and turn it back on).

If the call still fails after these steps, there may be a deeper issue with your device or account.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. - 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.

title: Cannot sign in to your account
body_text:
# Cannot sign in to your account

If you cannot log in, follow these steps to get back into your Northline Wireless account.

## Reset your password

1. Open the My Northline app or go to northline.example and tap **Forgot password**.
2. Enter the email address linked to your account.
3. Follow the link sent to your email to create a new password.
4. Choose a password you can remember, but that is hard for others to guess.

*If you enter the wrong password five times, your account will be locked for 30 minutes.* Wait until the lock period ends before trying again.

## Use the one-time code

A one-time code is a short number sent to your phone or email that lets you prove you own the account.

1. After resetting the password, you will be asked for a one-time code.
2. Check your phone's messages or your email for the code.
3. Enter the code within **10 minutes**; each code expires after that time.

If the code does not arrive:

1. Make sure your phone shows a good signal (the bars that indicate connection strength).
2. Request a new code by tapping **Resend code**.
3. Wait a moment and check your messages again.

## When you are locked out

1. After a lock, wait **30 minutes** before trying again.
2. During the wait, you can still use your phone for calls and texts; you just cannot sign in to the account.
3. When the lock expires, repeat the password reset or one-time code steps above.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support from any Northline phone by dialing **611**, or from any other phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is available **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

title: Not receiving verification codes
body_text:
# Not receiving verification codes

If you are not getting the text message with a verification code, follow these steps to fix the problem.

## Check your phone and signal
1. Turn your phone off. Hold the power button until the power menu appears, then select **Power off**.
2. Wait a few seconds, then turn the phone back on. This is called a restart and can clear temporary glitches.
3. Look at the signal bars at the top of the screen. If you see few or no bars, move to a place with better coverage. A strong signal helps the code reach your phone.

## Make sure short-code messages are allowed
A verification code is sent as a **short code** text (a message from a 5-digit number). Some phones can block these messages.
1. Open your messaging app.
2. Go to the app's **Settings** or **Options** menu.
3. Find the section called **Blocked numbers** or **Spam filter**.
4. Ensure that short-code numbers are not listed as blocked. If they are, remove them or turn off the block for short codes.

## Ask for a new code safely
1. Return to the website or app that asked for the code. Choose the option to **Resend code** or **Get a new code**.
2. Remember that each code is only valid for 10 minutes. Use it before it expires.
3. Never share the code with anyone, even if they call you. The code is for you only and should stay private.

If these steps do not solve the issue, you may need further assistance.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support from your phone by dialing **611**, or from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or online at **northline.example**.

title: The My Northline app is not working

Call Northline Wireless support from any Northline phone by dialing **611**, or from any other phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account online at **northline.example**.

title: Spot a scam text
body_text:
# Spot a scam text

Scam texts try to steal your personal information. This guide shows how to recognize them and what to do right away.

## What a scam text looks like

A scam text may say it is from Northline Wireless and ask for a PIN (personal identification number), password, or card number. Northline never asks for any of these details by text. The message might also contain a link that you did not expect. If the text feels urgent or promises a prize, it is likely a scam.

## What you should NOT do

1. Do not click any link in the message.
2. Do not reply with personal information such as a PIN, password, or credit-card number.
3. Do not forward the text to a friend or family member unless you are sure it is safe.

## How to report and protect yourself

1. Open the message on your phone.
2. Use the "forward" option in your messaging app.
3. Enter **7726** as the recipient. This short code is free to use.
4. Send the message.
5. After you have forwarded it, delete the original text from your phone.

Forwarding the text helps Northline investigate the scam and warn other customers. Deleting it removes the risk of accidentally tapping a bad link later.

## Need more help?

Call Northline support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at northline.example.

title: Calls pretending to be Northline
body_text:
# Calls pretending to be Northline

If you get a phone call that says it is from Northline and asks for personal information, it is likely a scam.

## How to recognize a fake call
Northline will **never** call you to ask for your full Social Security number (the nine-digit number the government uses to track earnings), your account PIN (a personal identification number you set to protect your account), or a verification code (a short number sent to you to prove you own the phone).
If the caller asks for any of these, the call is not from Northline.

## What to do if you receive a fake call
1. Hang up the phone.
2. Dial **611** from your Northline phone. This connects you directly to Northline support.
3. If you cannot use your Northline phone, call **1-800-555-0199** from any phone.
4. Tell the support agent that you received a suspicious call and what information, if any, you shared.

## Protect your account after a fake call
1. Open the **My Northline** app on your phone.
2. Go to the settings menu and select **Change PIN**. Follow the prompts to set a new, secret PIN that you have not used before.
3. In the same settings area, find **Number Lock** and turn it on. Number Lock stops anyone from using your phone number to make calls or send messages without your permission.

These steps keep your account safe even if a scammer heard some of your details.

## Need more help?
You can reach Northline support by dialing **611** from a Northline phone or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

title: Accessibility services
body_text:
# Accessibility services

Northline Wireless offers tools to help you read your bill and stay in touch, even if you have a hearing or vision challenge.

## Get large-print or braille bills for free

You can ask for a bill that is printed in large letters or in braille at no extra cost.

1. Open the **My Northline** app or go to **northline.example** and sign in.
2. Tap **Account** then **Billing preferences**.
3. Choose **Large-print bill** or **Braille bill** and select **Request**.
4. Save the change. Your next monthly bill will arrive in the format you chose.

If you prefer, you can also call support (see below) and ask a representative to set the request for you.

## Use real-time text on your phone

Real-time text (RTT) lets you type messages that are sent instantly as you type, so you can talk and read at the same time. Most recent phones support RTT.

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Find **Accessibility** (this section helps you use the phone if you have a disability).
3. Tap **Real-time text** and turn the switch **On**.
4. When you call someone, you will see a **RTT** button; tap it to start typing your words.

## Contact support with the 711 relay service

If you need help and cannot speak on the phone, you can use the 711 relay service. The relay service connects you to a live operator who types what you say and reads what the operator types back to you.

1. Dial **711** on any phone.
2. When the relay operator answers, tell them you need **Northline Wireless** support.
3. The operator will connect you to Northline support.
4. You can also call Northline support directly by dialing **611** from a Northline phone or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

Call Northline support at **611** (from a Northline phone) or **1-800-555-0199** (any phone). You can also use the **711 relay service** for a typed conversation. Support is available **7 a.m. - 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.

title: Hearing aid compatibility
body_text:
# Hearing aid compatibility

Many Northline phones work with hearing aids. Look for an M3 or T4 rating or higher.

## Find a compatible phone
1. Check the phone's specifications on the box or online listing.
2. Look for a rating that says **M3**, **M4**, **T4**, or higher.
   - **M rating** tells how well the phone's microphone works with hearing aids that use a microphone.
   - **T rating** tells how well the phone works with hearing aids that have a telecoil (a small coil that picks up magnetic signals).
3. Choose a phone that meets at least M3 or T4 if you need reliable sound.

## Turn on the hearing-aid setting
1. Open the **Settings** app on your phone.
2. Tap **Accessibility** (this section helps people with disabilities use the phone).
3. Find **Hearing aid compatibility** or **HAC** and switch it **On**.
4. The phone may ask you to restart; follow the prompt.

## Return a phone that doesn't work well
1. If the phone does not work well with your hearing aid, you can return it.
2. Contact Northline support within **30 days** of purchase.
3. Ask for a return label or visit a Northline store.
4. Pack the phone securely and send it back. You will receive a refund once the phone is received and inspected.

## Need more help?
Call Northline support at **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or online at northline.example.

title: Connect hearing aids by Bluetooth
body_text:
# Connect hearing aids by Bluetooth
You can link your hearing aids to your phone so the sound goes straight to them.

## Prepare your phone
1. Open the **Settings** app on your phone.
2. Find **Bluetooth** and turn it on. (Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology that lets devices talk to each other.)
3. Stay in Settings and tap **Accessibility**.
4. Choose **Hearing devices**. This screen lets you add hearing aids.

## Put the hearing aids in pairing mode
1. Open the battery door on each hearing aid.
2. Close the door again. This usually puts the aid into **pairing mode** - a state where it looks for a nearby Bluetooth device.
3. Wait a few seconds for the aid to be ready. You may see a flashing light indicating it is searching.

## Connect the devices
1. On the phone, you will see a list of nearby Bluetooth devices.
2. Look for the name of your hearing aid in the list.
3. Tap the name to select it.
4. If a confirmation prompt appears, tap **Connect**.
5. When the phone says the connection is successful, your hearing aids are ready to use.

You can now listen to calls, music, and other audio directly through your hearing aids.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

title: Make the screen easier to read
body_text:
# Make the screen easier to read

You can change the size of the text and make the screen clearer. This helps you read messages, emails, and apps without squinting.

## Change the font size

1. Open **Settings** - the app with a gear icon.
2. Tap **Display**.
3. Choose **Font size**.
4. Move the slider left or right. Sliding to the right makes the letters larger.
5. When the size looks good, tap the back arrow to exit.

*Font size* means how big the letters appear on the screen.

## Adjust the overall display size

1. In **Settings**, stay in the **Display** menu.
2. Tap **Display size** (sometimes called **Screen zoom**).
3. Move the slider toward the right to make everything on the screen larger, not just the text.
4. Press the back button when you are satisfied.

*Display size* changes the size of icons, buttons, and other items, so they are easier to tap.

## Turn on bold text and high-contrast mode

1. Open **Settings** and go to **Accessibility** - this section helps people use the phone more easily.
2. Tap **Bold text** and switch it on. The letters become thicker and stand out more.
3. Tap **High contrast** and turn it on. This adds a darker background to text and icons, making them easier to see.

*Accessibility* is a group of options that improve how you interact with the phone.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support from your phone by dialing **611**. If you are using another phone, dial **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage settings in the My Northline app or online at northline.example.

title: Use a screen reader
body_text:
# Use a screen reader

A screen reader reads what is on your phone out loud. It helps you use the phone without looking at the screen.

## What a screen reader does

A screen reader speaks the words on the screen. On Android phones it is called **TalkBack**. On iPhones it is called **VoiceOver**. Both read the screen aloud as you tap or swipe. The My Northline app works with TalkBack and VoiceOver, so you can manage your account with sound.

## Turn on TalkBack (Android)

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Scroll down and tap **Accessibility**.
3. Tap **TalkBack**.
4. Switch the toggle to **On**.
5. Follow any on-screen prompts to confirm.

TalkBack will now read everything you touch.

## Turn on VoiceOver (iPhone)

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Accessibility**.
3. Tap **VoiceOver**.
4. Turn the switch to **On**.
5. A short tutorial will play; listen and follow the directions.

VoiceOver will now speak the items on your screen.

## Using the My Northline app

1. Open the **My Northline** app.
2. TalkBack or VoiceOver will announce each button as you move your finger.
3. Double-tap (Android) or double-click (iPhone) to select a highlighted item.
4. Swipe left or right to move between screens.
5. Use the spoken prompts to check your balance, change a plan, or view usage.

You can perform most account tasks without looking at the phone.

## Need more help?

Call Northline Wireless support from your phone by dialing **611**, or from any phone at **1-800-555-0199**. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

title: Contact Northline support

title: Check coverage in your area
body_text:
# Check coverage in your area
Find out if Northline Wireless works at your home or work.

## How to check coverage
1. Open a web browser on any device.
2. Go to **northline.example/coverage**.
3. You will see a box that asks for an address.
4. Type the street address, city, and zip code where you want to check.
5. Press **Enter** or click the **Search** button.
6 The map will show the signal strength for that location. Darker colors mean stronger signal.

## Why indoor signal can be weaker
*Coverage* means the area where the network can reach your phone. Buildings, walls, and metal can block the signal. The map shows the strongest signal that can be seen outdoors. Inside a house or office, the signal may be lower than the map suggests.

## Using Wi-Fi calling when indoor signal is weak
Wi-Fi calling lets your phone make calls and send texts over your home internet instead of the cellular signal.

1. Open the **Settings** app on your phone.
2. Find **Phone** or **Calls** (the name may vary).
3. Tap **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn it on.
4. Follow any prompts to confirm your address for emergency services.

When Wi-Fi calling is on, you can talk and text even if the cellular signal is weak inside your building.

## Need more help?
Call Northline Wireless support by dialing **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time, every day. You can also manage your account in the My Northline app or at **northline.example**.

title: Calling 911
body_text:
# Calling 911

If you need help fast, you can dial 911 even if your Northline Wireless service is suspended or your plan has no minutes left.

## 911 works without active minutes
When you call 911, the network treats the call as an emergency.
- The call will go through even if your account is paused.
- It also works if you have used all your talk minutes.

You do not need to worry about your plan balance in an emergency.

## Using Wi-Fi calling for 911
If your phone is connected to Wi-Fi and you have Wi-Fi calling turned on, 911 will still connect. The call uses the emergency address you saved in your phone settings. Keep that address current so responders know where to go.

1. Open your phone's Settings app.
2. Find **Wi-Fi Calling** (often under **Phone** or **Connections**).
3. Tap **Emergency Address** or **Location**.
4. Enter your full street address, city, and zip code.
5. Save the changes.

If you move, repeat these steps to update the address.

## What to do if 911 does not connect
1. Stay calm and try the call again.
2. If you have Wi-Fi, make sure you are still connected.
3. If the call still fails, use a landline or a neighbor's phone if possible.
4. After the emergency, contact Northline support to check your service settings.

## Keep your emergency address up to date in the app
You can also update the address in the My Northline app.

1. Open the **My Northline** app.
2. Tap **Profile** or **Account Settings**.
3. Choose **Emergency Address**.
4. Edit the address and save.

## Need more help?
Call Northline support at **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. to 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day.

title: How Northline protects your account information
body_text:
# How Northline protects your account information

Northline Wireless keeps your call records, usage and billing details safe. Only you and people you approve can see this information.

## What information is protected
Northline treats call records (the list of numbers you called), usage details (how much data or talk time you used) and billing details (your monthly bill) as private. These items are stored securely and are not shared without your permission.

## How we verify you before sharing details
When you call support, the representative will ask for your account PIN. A PIN is a personal identification number you set to prove who you are.
1. Dial **611** from your Northline phone, or **1-800-555-0199** from any other phone.
2. Wait for a support agent to answer.
3. The agent will ask you to enter or tell them your account PIN.
4. If the PIN matches, the agent can discuss your account. If it does not match, they cannot share any information.

Only the account owner and any authorized users you have added can receive account details. Authorized users are people you have given permission to view or manage the account, such as a family member.

## How you can keep your account safe
1. Choose a PIN that is hard for others to guess. Avoid birthdays or simple sequences.
2. Keep your PIN private. Do not write it down where others can see it.
3. Use the **My Northline** app or log in at **northline.example** to review your account and add or remove authorized users.
4. If you suspect someone else knows your PIN, change it right away in the app or by calling support.

## Need more help?
Call Northline support at **611** from a Northline phone or **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. Support is open **7 a.m. - 9 p.m. Central Time**, every day. You can also manage your account in the **My Northline** app or at **northline.example**.
